desc:
Discover how Professor Tom Ellis is rewriting DNA to programme microbes to grow sustainable materials and help build a bio-based future.

Living Code, Living Materials: How Synthetic Biology is Rewriting the Future

Abstract:

S cience has focused on reading the code of life to understand how living organisms work, but today, bioengineers are writing that code. By rewriting DNA in organisms like yeast and bacteria, we can transform simple microbes into programmable micro-factories. title: GATP Seminar – Ed Segal (UCL)
desc: In N=(2,2) Calabi-Yau GLSMs it should be possible to transfer B-branes between different phases, or to put it another way, two CY varieties which arise as different GIT quotients of the same space should be derived equivalent. For abelian gauge groups this is well-understood but the non-abelian case is still very hard. I’ll discuss the example of stratified Mukai flops which is well-known as a difficult test case. In recent work (with Wei Tseu) we found a simple geometric construction of the Fourier-Mukai kernel for the derived equivalence in this example.

desc:

Title : Sensitivity of Distributionally Robust Optimization in the Adapted Bures–Wasserstein Space

Abstract : The adapted Wasserstein distance provides a natural framework for comparing stochastic processes while accounting for their temporal structure and the flow of information, especially for the purpose of dynamic stochastic optimization in a context of model uncertainty. When restricted to Gaussian processes, it gives rise to the adapted Bures–Wasserstein space, an analogue of the classical Bures–Wasserstein geometry in optimal transport. In this talk, I will present a complete geometric analysis of such space, and provide an explicit characterization of the solutions to the adapted transport problem. Title: Geometric Neural Operators for Machine Learning Probabilistic Weather Prediction

title: Structures Seminar: Seismic Behaviour and Design of the Linked Column Steel Frame System for Rapid Return to Occupancy
desc:
Abstract:

The Linked Column Frame (LCF) is a new brace-free lateral structural steel system intended for rapid return to occupancy performance level. LCF is more resilient under a design level earthquake than the conventional approaches. The structural system consists of moment frames for gravity that combine with closely spaced dual columns (LC) interconnected with bolted links for the lateral system. The LC links are sacrificial and intended to be replaced following a design level earthquake. The centerpiece of this work was a unique full-scale experiment using hybrid testing; a combination of physical test of a critical sub-system tied to a numerical model of the building frame. Hybrid testing allows for full scale study at the system level, accounting for the uncertainties via…

title: Control and Optimisation seminar – Gargoei Loke (Durham)
desc:
Title

Analyzing the Flexibility Afforded by Smart Charging as a Multi-product Newsvendor with Indifferent Demand

Abstract

In this paper, we take the perspective of a smart charging operator, who needs to make a day-ahead bid on the amount of energy required on the next day, before the demand for smart charging materializes. The demand comprises the quantity of vehicles, as well as the heterogeneous degree of flexibility that each vehicle affords the charging operator, both of which are stochastic at the point of making the day-ahead bid. We cast this problem as a multi-product newsvendor problem with demand flexibility, in the form of product indifference. title: HEP seminar: Samuel Eriksen (Bristol) – Search for high-energy dark matter interactions with the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment
desc: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) dark matter search experiment, a dual-phase xenon time projection chamber operating at the Sanford Underground Research Facility in Lead, South Dakota, USA, has demonstrated the world’s leading sensitivity to searches for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs). LZ’s exceptional sensitivity enables this new search for dark matter interactions that can produce high-energy (O(100) keV) nuclear recoils, a region where LZ’s modelled backgrounds produce much less than one event in the investigated 2.84 tonne-years exposure. Through a model-agnostic non-relativistic effective field theory (NR-EFT) framework, signals arising from vector, axial, and dipole WIMP-nucleon couplings are probed. This seminar will describe the experiment and the results from the most recent…
